reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is a no-op with no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — nothing improper is being proposed to the counterparty.

The cited text supports compliance on the data limb: Section 9.7 (p0517–p0518) is a termination-triggered, mutual return-or-destroy right at the requesting Party's written election, with written certification of destruction and retention limited to one archival/legal copy plus automated back-ups. That is the rule's 'return, then delete and certify' construct and is well clear of the walk-away ('no data return, or immediate deletion').

The transition limb is addressed with real cites (Article 12.7 reversion, Section 12.6.1(c), the post-termination sell-off window in 12.10.2, surviving record/copy rights in 3.8.5, and the forward-looking Manufacturing Technology Transfer with assistance in 3.5/3.8.2(a)/4.5.2). The direction analysis is sound: on termination rights in the Licensed Compounds revert to Harpoon, so post-termination assistance necessarily runs from AbbVie to Harpoon; inserting a Vendor-side 'return Customer Data' clause would be inapposite in a development/option/licence agreement where the counterparty is not a processor of our service data.

The failed deterministic 'data return/transition present' check is a phrasing-match heuristic; the agreement uses 'Return of Confidential Information', 'destroy … and confirm such destruction in writing', and reversion/technology-transfer language rather than the playbook's services/hosting vocabulary, so the regex miss is not probative here.

Shortfalls versus the preferred wording are correctly noted rather than flagged: 'as soon as reasonably practicable' instead of a fixed 30-day window, no machine-readable-format requirement, and Harpoon's election to have AbbVie-generated data destroyed under 12.6.1(c). These are sub-elements short of preferred, not failures of the fallback, so no redline is the right call under the classification semantics.
